newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas little changed, softer in Midwest.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas little changed, softer in Midwest.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were steady to slightly softer Thursday, pressured by a lower-than-expected storage drawdown in AGA's report but supported by cooler forecasts next week, sources said.
Several sources also said withdrawals were continuing at a steady pace today, adding a substantial withdrawal rate will likely appear in AGA's next storage report.

Gulf prices were softer early in the mid-$3.30s but then recovered by a few cents to about $3.40 due to six- to 10-day forecasts calling for below to much below-normal temperatures throughout most of the U.S., excluding the East Coast.
Adding some short-term strength to the market was news that one of TransCanada Pipelines three 30-inch gas pipelines ruptured late Wednesday near Vermillion Bay in western Ontario.
However, the company said no deliveries were affected since they were able to re-route the gas along an adjacent pipeline.
In the eastern market areas, prices were also fairly steady in the low-$4 area at the New York city-gate.
Northeast Utilities said Thursday it has restored electricity service to nearly all of its electricity customers in New Hampshire, Connecticut and western Massachusetts following last Sunday's storm.
However, forecasters said another storm is moving toward the Northeast and may bring precipitation and wind to the area this weekend.
In the Midcontinent, prices eased by about three cents to the low-to-mid $3.30s as mild weather continued in the producing region.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices were flat in the mid-$3.20s in light activity.
One source speculated that most buyers were fairly balanced after this past bidweek, resulting in a weak demand in the aftermarket.
At the southern California border, traders reported closing deals in the $3.45-3.50 range, up only about two cents, as cooler air moved into the western U.S.
